game.welcome: {{firm}} is founded! The company number is on its way, the coffee machine is leased and the LinkedIn post has 14 likes.

staff.leftMany: {{count}} employees quit this quarter. The farewell cake was dry.
staff.arrived: {{count}} new consultants showed up with shiny laptops and high hopes.
staff.talentSpotted: {{name}} has turned out to be a real talent. A future star in {{discipline}}?
staff.promiseKept: {{name}} got the growth you promised in the career talk.
staff.promiseBroken: {{name}} has quit. The promise from the career talk was never kept.
staff.promoted: {{name}} has been promoted to star consultant in {{discipline}}.
staff.courseDone_one: {{name}} has finished the course and has a new certificate on LinkedIn.
staff.courseDone_other: {{count}} people have finished their courses and have new certificates on LinkedIn.

tender.noBids: Nobody bid on the tender from {{customer}}. Procurement is taking a long lunch.
tender.noneGoodEnough: {{customer}} turned down every bid on its tender. None were good enough.
tender.playerRejected: {{customer}} turned down your bid. The quality wasn't there, however nice the cover page.
tender.playerRejectedCapacity: {{customer}} turned down your bid. You didn't have enough people free, and they checked.
tender.playerWon: You won the tender at {{customer}}! {{bidders}} firms bid. {{strong}}
tender.playerWonFramework: You were ranked #{{rank}} on the framework agreement at {{customer}}. {{strong}}
tender.playerLost: You lost the tender at {{customer}} to {{firm}}. {{weak}}
tender.playerLostBoth: You lost the tender at {{customer}} to {{firm}}. {{weak}} {{strong}}
tender.awarded: {{firm}} won the tender at {{customer}}, beating {{bidders}} others.
tender.frameworkAwarded: {{firm}} tops the framework agreement at {{customer}}. {{bidders}} firms fought for a spot.

contract.terminatedUnhappy: {{customer}} has terminated its contract with {{firm}}. "We're going in a different direction."
contract.ended: The engagement at {{customer}} has ended. Customer satisfaction: {{satisfaction}} out of 100.
contract.renewed: {{customer}} extends the engagement by {{count}} quarters. They were happy!
contract.renegotiated: {{customer}} accepts the new rate: ×{{rate}}. Procurement sighed audibly.
contract.renegotiateFailed: {{customer}} says no to the new rate, and will remember you asked.
contract.cancelled: You have cancelled the contract with {{customer}}. The exit fee is paid.
contract.upsellFailed: {{customer}} has no budget for more people right now.

shady.poachSuccess: {{name}} has moved from {{from}} to {{to}}. Apparently it happened over an IPA.
shady.poachFailed: The afterwork with people from {{from}} only produced a large bar tab.
shady.rumorVictim: There are rumours about you going around. Nobody knows who started them.
shady.dnLeak: Business daily exposé: "How {{firm}} really works". It's behind a paywall, but everyone has read it.

scandal.spy_bids: {{firm}} caught snooping on competitors' bids. Fine: {{fine}}.
scandal.spy_salaries: {{firm}} has been collecting payslips from {{target}}. Nobody found it charming.
scandal.plant_mole: Mole exposed! {{firm}} had a "trainee" at {{target}} for four months. Fine: {{fine}}.
scandal.afterwork_poach: {{firm}}'s afterwork was a bit too obvious. {{target}} is not impressed.
scandal.silent_outsource: {{customer}} found out that {{firm}}'s team was in a different time zone. Contract terminated. Fine: {{fine}}.
scandal.cv_pad: "Kubernetes expert since 2009"? {{customer}} checked {{firm}}'s CVs. The contract is gone.
scandal.ghost_cv: {{firm}} offered consultants who don't exist. {{customer}} noticed. Fine: {{fine}}.
scandal.bait_and_switch: {{customer}} got juniors instead of the promised seniors from {{firm}}. The relationship is frosty.
scandal.rumor: Turns out the rumours about {{target}} came from {{firm}}. Awkward.
scandal.dn_leak: The leak about {{target}} was traced back to {{firm}}. Fine: {{fine}}.
scandal.linkedin_post: {{firm}}'s LinkedIn post about {{target}} was widely shared for all the wrong reasons.

award.coffee_machine: Best Coffee Machine in the Industry {{year}}: {{firm}}.
award.creative_timesheets: Most Creative Timesheets {{year}}: {{firm}}. The jury was impressed and slightly worried.

trend.ended: The "{{trend}}" trend is over. Everyone pretends they were never into it.

firm.acquired: {{firm}} acquired a small {{discipline}} agency. The business cards have already been reprinted.
firm.bankrupt: {{firm}} has gone bankrupt. The foosball table is for sale online.
firm.playerBankrupt: {{firm}} has gone bankrupt. The receiver has taken over the foosball table.
firm.bankWarning: The bank called. They were polite, but noticeably less warm than before.
firm.acquiredBy: {{buyer}} has bought {{firm}}. The logo will be "kept for now".

mission.done: Goal reached: {{mission}}. The board applauds politely.

ipo.listed: {{firm}} is listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange! The founders rang the bell and someone filmed it vertically.
ipo.miss: The quarter came in weaker than the last. Shareholders are disappointed, and it shows in the corridors.
ipo.beat: A better quarter than last time. Shareholders are happy, at least until next quarter.

kept.fullTeam: {{customer}} got the whole team from day one, just as you promised. They noticed.
kept.phased: The phased start at {{customer}} went as promised. They like predictable.
kept.discovery: The discovery phase at {{customer}} is done, and they're glad someone asked first. Full rates from now on.

broken.fullTeam: You promised {{customer}} the whole team from the start, then filled the gaps with contractors. They made a note of it.
broken.phased: You promised {{customer}} a phased start, but contractors filled more than half the seats.

crisis.buried: “{{crisis}}” is in the drawer. For now.

ended.good: “{{crisis}}” is over, and you came out of it well.
ended.ok: “{{crisis}}” is over. It could have been worse.
ended.bad: “{{crisis}}” is over, but it left a mark.

crisis.exposed: It came out: “{{crisis}}” is in the papers.
crisis.exposedRival: Exposed: {{firm}} tried to hush something up. Now it's in the papers.

announcements.mug_meeting_room: Would {{name}} please collect their mug from meeting room Fjord View.
announcements.friday_beer_alcohol_free: A reminder that today's Friday beer is alcohol-free. Nobody knows why.
announcements.fridge_cleanup: The fridge will be emptied on Friday at 3 pm. This includes last year's yoghurt.
announcements.printer_on_fire: The printer on the third floor is not on fire. It just smells like that.
announcements.wifi_password: New Wi-Fi password: Password123. IT asks that you stop asking.
announcements.standup_standing: A reminder that stand-up means standing up. It's in the name.
announcements.cake_in_kitchen: There's cake in the kitchen. Nobody knows whose birthday it is. Eat anyway.
announcements.timesheet_reminder: Timesheets are due Friday. Yes, including last month's.
announcements.lost_macbook_charger: Has anyone seen a USB-C charger? It's white. They're all white.
announcements.fire_drill: Fire drill at 2 pm. Please don't bring your laptop and keep coding in the stairwell.
announcements.parking_spot: {{name}} has parked in the CEO's spot. Again.
announcements.jira_down: Jira is down. Productivity is up 40 percent.
announcements.someone_microwaved_fish: To whoever microwaved fish: we know who you are.
announcements.meeting_room_hostage: Meeting room Ocean Glimpse is booked by a meeting that never ends. Send coffee.
announcements.sprint_retro_cake: The retro cake was eaten before the retro started. This will be raised at the retro.
announcements.dress_code: Reminder: a hoodie is not client-meeting attire. Unless the client is wearing a hoodie.
announcements.intern_lost: Has anyone seen the intern? He went to get coffee on Tuesday.
announcements.ceo_birthday: It's the CEO's birthday. The card is at reception. Write something nice.
announcements.coffee_beans_out: We're out of coffee beans. The budget for new ones arrives next quarter.
announcements.fagdag_room: The tech day continues in the canteen. Bring your own chair and strong opinions on TypeScript.
announcements.kombucha_on_tap: The kombucha tap has been refilled. Don't ask who ordered it.
announcements.bench_reminder: Reminder: if you're on the bench, update your CV. And maybe once more.
announcements.overtime_pizza: Pizza for everyone working late tonight. So, everyone.
announcements.compliance_tor: Tor from compliance would like a word with everyone. One at a time. Door closed.
announcements.shredder_busy: The shredder is busy until 5 pm. Please don't ask.
announcements.journalists_in_lobby: There's someone from the business press in reception. Say we're at a team-building event.
announcements.morale_survey: The wellbeing survey is out. It's completely anonymous. Completely.
announcements.pingpong_final: The ping-pong final is at 4 pm. The prize is glory and a hot-dog voucher.
announcements.new_office_plants: The office has new plants. They're real. We checked.
announcements.elevator_pitch: The lift is full of consultants practising their elevator pitch. Take the stairs.
announcements.small_office: Reminder: office space is limited. Please don't take video calls in the loo.
announcements.cash_low: Finance asks everyone to consider whether they really need new Post-it notes.
announcements.printer_toner: The printer says it's out of yellow. We only print in black and white. It says so anyway.
announcements.teams_status: Reminder: a green status in Teams does not mean you're working. But it helps.
announcements.dishwasher: The dishwasher is clean. It has been clean since Tuesday. Someone has to empty it.
announcements.reply_all: Please do not reply all to the email about not replying all.
announcements.standing_desk: The standing desk on the fourth floor is stuck in the up position. Its owner says it was a choice.
announcements.lunch_menu: Today's lunch is 'Asian-inspired'. The chef won't say what inspired it.
announcements.badge_forgotten: Could someone let in the colleague at the door? They've been standing there since 8:15.
announcements.mute_button: To whoever just asked 'am I on mute?' in the all-hands: no.
announcements.password_policy: New password policy: at least 16 characters, one number and one feeling.
announcements.okr_workshop: The OKR workshop is postponed. The objective is to set an objective for when to hold it.
announcements.whiteboard: Please don't wipe the whiteboard in meeting room Northern Lights. Nobody knows what it means, but it looks important.
announcements.slack_channels: We now have 214 Slack channels. A channel has been created to discuss this.
announcements.air_con: The air con is set to 21 degrees. This is a compromise nobody is happy with.
announcements.fruit_bowl: The fruit bowl has been refilled. The bananas are already gone. The apples will survive, as usual.
announcements.lost_airpod: A single AirPod has been found at reception. It misses its partner.
announcements.calendar_invite: Everyone has received a calendar invite with no title, agenda or room. Please attend.
announcements.code_freeze: The code freeze starts Friday. That does not mean you can deploy on Thursday at 11:59 pm.
announcements.hackathon: Hackathon sign-up is open. Theme: 'something with AI'. The prize is another idea.
announcements.coat_rack: The jacket that has hung in the cloakroom since the last reorganisation will be given away on Friday. Last chance.
announcements.microwave_queue: The microwave queue starts at 11:28. Please do not heat lasagne for eleven minutes.
announcements.agile_coach: The agile coach would like to remind you that there are no stupid questions. Only long ones.
announcements.bike_room: The bike room is full. Someone has parked a tandem. We don't know who the two of them are.
announcements.plastic_plant: The plant at reception is plastic. Please stop watering it.
announcements.confluence_updated: The Confluence docs have been updated. For the first time since they were written.
announcements.mechanical_keyboard: To whoever has the mechanical keyboard in the open-plan office: we hear you. All the time.
announcements.vpn_slow: The VPN is slow today. IT suggests working a bit slower too.
announcements.quiz_night: Quiz night on Thursday. Teams of four. Questions on everything except Kubernetes.
announcements.phone_booth: The phone booths are for phone calls. Not naps. However good the nap was.
announcements.expense_receipts: Expense claims without receipts will not be approved. Not even with a drawing of the receipt.
announcements.coffee_machine_options: The new coffee machine has 34 options. They all come out as latte.
announcements.laptop_updates: Laptops will update tonight. Save everything and say goodbye to your tabs.
announcements.star_podcast: {{name}} has started a podcast. Everyone is invited to listen. Ideally more than once.
announcements.star_linkedin: {{name}} has posted on LinkedIn again. Please like it and it will pass.
announcements.star_deep_work: {{name}} has booked every meeting room for 'deep work'. Everyone else is working shallowly in the canteen.
announcements.star_sourdough: {{name}} has brought a sourdough starter to the kitchen. It has a name. Don't eat it.
announcements.new_year_gym: The gym is full this week. Next week it will be back to normal.
announcements.easter_quiz: The Easter quiz is ready. The correct answer to every question is 'it depends'.
announcements.may_17: The office closes early before Constitution Day. National dress is not required at the morning meeting.
announcements.back_from_holiday: Welcome back from holiday. You have 1,400 unread emails. None of them matter any more.
announcements.summer_students: The summer students have taken over the third floor. They've already refactored the coffee machine.
announcements.christmas_party: Christmas party sign-up closes Friday. What happens at the Christmas party ends up on Slack.
announcements.secret_santa: Secret Santa names have been drawn. The budget is 200 kroner. Yes, even if you got the boss.
announcements.budget_season: Budgeting for next year has begun. All figures are provisional, especially the good ones.
announcements.legal_hold: Legal would like to remind you that emails are archived. All of them. Forever.
announcements.lawyers_back: The lawyers are back. They brought their own coffee. That's a bad sign.
announcements.whistleblower_channel: The whistleblowing channel is open around the clock. It's also completely anonymous. Regards, Tor.
announcements.compliance_bored: Compliance has nothing to do and has started auditing the cake rota.
announcements.media_training: Mandatory media training at 1 pm. Exercise one: say 'no comment' with a smile.
announcements.trophy_shelf: The trophy shelf is full. We've ordered a new shelf. And a duster.
announcements.new_logo: Marketing is working on a new logo. Apparently the old one did something wrong.
announcements.overdraft_hello: The overdraft would like to remind you that it exists. It says hello.
announcements.weekend_open: The office is open at the weekend too. Not that anyone has to. Just so you know.
announcements.bench_workshop: Everyone on the bench is invited to an internal workshop on getting off the bench.
announcements.record_morale: The wellbeing survey shows record morale. Management asks that we don't tell the competition.
announcements.exit_interviews: HR has booked a room for exit interviews all week. This is entirely coincidental.
announcements.lunch_talk_monads: Lunch talk today: 'Monads for everyone'. Everyone is welcome.
announcements.build_server: Does anyone know how the build server works? The person who knew has left.
announcements.company_choir: The company choir rehearses in the canteen at 4 pm. Please don't sing along. Actually, do.
announcements.social_two_came: There was a social get-together in the canteen yesterday. Thanks to the two who came.
announcements.name_tags: We're now big enough for name tags. Write clearly. And not 'The Boss'.
announcements.all_hands_coffee: The all-hands will be held by the coffee machine. Everyone is present. Everyone gets a turn.
announcements.share_price_screen: The share price is now shown on the screen at reception. Please don't stand and watch it all day.
announcements.quiet_period: We're in the quiet period before results. That includes the kitchen.
announcements.corner_office: The new corner office is finished. It's a meeting room. Stop arguing.
announcements.business_cards: We have business cards. They're misprinted. We're using them anyway.
announcements.strategy_2037: The 2037 strategy is ready. It was written by AI and is very sure of itself.
announcements.new_premises: Welcome to the new premises. Wi-Fi arrives next week. The chairs the week after.
announcements.offshore_standup: The morning meeting with the offshore team has moved to 6:30 am. In the interest of fairness.

overworked.1: I haven't seen my family since the last sprint.
overworked.2: I've started dreaming in Jira tickets.
overworked.3: Three meetings at once isn't multitasking. It's a cry for help.
overworked.4: When did we last have a Friday that was actually a Friday?
overworked.5: There isn't a single free slot in my calendar before Easter.
overworked.6: I billed 46 hours this week. My body has sent an invoice back.
overworked.7: My cat thinks I'm someone who drops by in the evenings.
overworked.8: I replied "have a nice weekend" to an email on Tuesday. It was from me.
overworked.9: Can someone else take tomorrow's stand-up? I have three other stand-ups.
overworked.10: I've forgotten what my hobby was. I think it involved bread.

bench_bored.1: I haven't billed in three weeks and I've started painting the office.
bench_bored.2: I've refactored my own dotfiles four times now.
bench_bored.3: Does anyone have a project? Any project? I know Excel.
bench_bored.4: I've read the entire staff handbook. There's a typo on page 14.
bench_bored.5: Today I learned Rust. Tomorrow it's Haskell. Send help.
bench_bored.6: I made the coffee machine faster. Nobody asked me to.
bench_bored.7: The bench is comfortable, but I miss the clients. Almost.
bench_bored.8: I built an internal app for booking lunch tables. There's no queue.
bench_bored.9: I've watered the plants so much they've started looking worried.
bench_bored.10: If I write one more blog post about "learning on the bench", I quit.

good_flow.1: Finally a project where things actually happen.
good_flow.2: We shipped yesterday and nothing broke. I don't fully trust it.
good_flow.3: The client said "thanks" in Slack. With an exclamation mark.
good_flow.4: I got into the zone today and forgot lunch. In a good way.
good_flow.5: The retro was short because nothing was wrong. Weird.
good_flow.6: It's nice working on something people actually use.
good_flow.7: We have a backlog that makes sense. I want to frame it.
good_flow.8: The demo went so well the product owner clapped. Alone, but still.
good_flow.9: I wonder if this is what they call "a sustainable pace".
good_flow.10: My team is actually really good. Don't tell them.

embarrassed.1: I don't tell people where I work at parties any more.
embarrassed.2: Mum called to ask if I was in the paper.
embarrassed.3: I took off my company hoodie on the underground.
embarrassed.4: My LinkedIn now just says "consultant". No company name.
embarrassed.5: The neighbour asked if we were "the ones from the news". I said we're a different firm.
embarrassed.6: The client met us in reception with a very neutral face.
embarrassed.7: I've gone back to saying I work "in IT".
embarrassed.8: It's hard to sell an agile mindset when you're on the front page.

suspicious.1: Why do we suddenly have an "external resource" in Manila answering my emails?
suspicious.2: Why are there three CVs in the bid from people I've never met?
suspicious.3: Management has started closing the meeting room door. We never do that.
suspicious.4: I was told "not to mention it" in the client meeting. Mention what?
suspicious.5: Someone ordered a shredder. A big one.
suspicious.6: There's a new line in the accounts called "miscellaneous, strategic".
suspicious.7: Tor from compliance looks more tired than usual.
suspicious.8: How do we know what Accentura is bidding before they do?

star_restless.1: {{name}} has updated their LinkedIn profile three times this week.
star_restless.2: {{name}} went to a "dentist appointment" in a suit yesterday.
star_restless.3: {{name}} said "if I'm still here by then" in the planning meeting.
star_restless.4: {{name}} has started taking personal things home. One a day.
star_restless.5: Headhunters call {{name}} so often it has its own ringtone.
star_restless.6: {{name}} has started talking very warmly about "new challenges".

underpaid.1: I think I'm underpaid. No, I know I am.
underpaid.2: My mate at Accentura has a car with heated seats. And a salary.
underpaid.3: I bill 1,700 an hour and bring a packed lunch. Something doesn't add up.
underpaid.4: My pay review lasted four minutes. Three of them were about the weather.
underpaid.5: I've seen the job ads. I know what other people earn.
underpaid.6: The fruit bowl is lovely, but it doesn't pay the rent.
underpaid.7: I worked out my hourly wage and got a bit sad.
underpaid.8: Is "we're like a family" a form of payment?

good_pay.1: The pay is actually pretty decent here.
good_pay.2: I checked the market and came back. It's good here.
good_pay.3: I bought a new bike and didn't even feel guilty.
good_pay.4: The boss gave me a raise before I asked. Is everything all right?
good_pay.5: The headhunter asked what I earn and hung up rather quickly.
good_pay.6: I've stopped opening job ads. That's a good sign.

no_learning.1: I haven't learned anything new since jQuery.
no_learning.2: Our last learning day was in 2019. It was about learning days.
no_learning.3: I learn more from YouTube comments than from work.
no_learning.4: The course I asked for is "under consideration". It has been for a year.
no_learning.5: Our practice group has one member. Me. We rarely meet.
no_learning.6: I've seen the same Kubernetes talk three times. All of them were mine.
no_learning.7: The conference budget covers a coffee at Starbucks, if we share.
no_learning.8: When they say "learning on the job", they mean I google things.

fagdag_good.1: The learning day was actually good. I understood almost everything.
fagdag_good.2: We had lightning talks today. Mine lasted five minutes and got two questions.
fagdag_good.3: I'm going to JavaZone and the firm is paying. I've been packing since March.
fagdag_good.4: The practice group built its own library. People actually use it.
fagdag_good.5: I learned more in today's code review than on a whole course.
fagdag_good.6: We have a book club for technical books. We even read them.
fagdag_good.7: The juniors gave talks, and the seniors took notes.
fagdag_good.8: The hackathon gave us three prototypes and one the client wants.

lonely.1: It's quiet in the office. Very quiet.
lonely.2: I had lunch with myself again. The conversation was poor.
lonely.3: Friday drinks are cancelled. They were cancelled last week too.
lonely.4: I don't know the names of half my colleagues.
lonely.5: I said "good morning" in Teams and nobody replied until two.
lonely.6: The ping-pong table has gathered dust. That's not a metaphor.
lonely.7: I've started talking to the plants. They're good listeners.
lonely.8: The Christmas party was replaced by a gift card. Worth 200 kroner.

great_colleagues.1: I like my colleagues. Is that allowed?
great_colleagues.2: Someone brought cake today for no reason. That's the best reason.
great_colleagues.3: We stayed after Friday drinks and solved a problem the client didn't know they had.
great_colleagues.4: When I'm stuck, someone always has time.
great_colleagues.5: We have a Slack channel just for pictures of dogs. It's very active.
great_colleagues.6: Friday's quiz was so close we demanded a rematch.
great_colleagues.7: I'm actually looking forward to Monday. Don't tell anyone.
great_colleagues.8: My team celebrated my birthday. I never told anyone when it is.

rival_sushi.2: Apparently {{firm}} gets a cabin in the mountains. A whole cabin.
rival_sushi.3: My old classmate at {{firm}} gets four learning days a month.
rival_sushi.4: {{firm}} has its own barista. I have a thermos.
rival_sushi.5: I saw the Christmas party photos from {{firm}}. They were in Lisbon.
rival_sushi.6: {{firm}} sends people to conferences in the US. We get a Teams webinar.

who_are_freelancers.1: Who are all these people without access cards?
who_are_freelancers.2: There's a freelancer in the Fjordgløtt meeting room. He's lived there since August.
who_are_freelancers.3: I was introduced to "Erik from the subcontractor" for the third time.
who_are_freelancers.4: The freelancers have their own Slack. Apparently it's much more fun.
who_are_freelancers.5: The client thinks he's one of us. We haven't corrected them.
who_are_freelancers.6: The freelancer bills more than me and hasn't been to a single learning day.

startup_vibes.1: It feels a bit like a startup. In a good way, mostly.
startup_vibes.2: There are so few of us that one pizza is enough. Almost.
startup_vibes.3: I'm the CTO, the product owner and in charge of the coffee machine.
startup_vibes.4: Everyone knows everything about everyone. That's both nice and slightly scary.
startup_vibes.5: The board meeting was held at the kitchen counter. It was efficient.
startup_vibes.6: We don't have HR yet, so we just talk to each other.

all_quiet.1: Everything is as it should be. Suspicious.
all_quiet.2: Nothing has been on fire for a while. Touch wood.
all_quiet.3: It's so calm I've started reading documentation.
all_quiet.4: I have nothing to complain about, and it makes me nervous.
all_quiet.5: The coffee is hot, the project is on track and nobody has called. What's going on?
all_quiet.6: A completely ordinary day. I'll enjoy it before something happens.

cash_tight.1: Why is lunch suddenly just bread and butter?
cash_tight.2: Management talks a lot about "cost awareness" these days.
cash_tight.3: This year's Christmas present is apparently "togetherness".
cash_tight.4: I was asked to print on both sides of the paper.
cash_tight.5: The accountant doesn't smile in the corridor any more.
cash_tight.6: We were told to bill for everything. Including our thoughts.

crisis_open.1: Every manager has their calendar blocked with "meeting". Just "meeting".
crisis_open.2: I don't know what's going on, but there's a lot of pizza in the boardroom.
crisis_open.3: Someone wrote "DO NOT TALK TO THE PRESS" on the whiteboard. Then rubbed it out.
crisis_open.4: The comms adviser has been here three days in a row.
crisis_open.5: We got an email saying "everything is under control". We've never had one of those before.
crisis_open.6: I've never seen the boss drink this much coffee.

big_firm.1: I don't know everyone's name any more. I smile and nod.
big_firm.2: We now have a team that makes templates for other templates.
big_firm.3: It takes three approvals to order a new monitor.
big_firm.4: The all-hands has got so big we need a microphone.
big_firm.5: Someone from another team said hello in the lift. Turns out we're on the same project.
big_firm.6: I miss when there were so few of us that everyone fitted round one table.

listed.1: I check the share price more often than the weather now.
listed.2: The quarterly report is the most exciting thing we read all year.
listed.3: Management has started saying "shareholder value" in perfectly normal sentences.
listed.4: My options are worth a holiday in the sun. Or a coffee, depending on the day.
listed.5: We were told not to comment on anything before the report. Not even lunch.

season_q1.1: It's been dark since November. I've forgotten what the sun looks like.
season_q1.2: My New Year's resolution was to write tests. It lasted nine days.
season_q1.3: I came to work on skis today. It wasn't on purpose.
season_q1.4: The budgets are new and the clients are optimistic. That lasts until March.
season_q1.5: Winter break is in two weeks and I've already gone into hibernation.
season_q1.6: Easter is coming, and every client wants everything delivered before it.

season_q2.1: The light is back, and suddenly everyone is incredibly productive.
season_q2.2: The 17 May parade went right past the office. We waved from the meeting room.
season_q2.3: Someone has put the garden furniture out on the roof terrace. We don't have a roof terrace.
season_q2.4: Everyone wants a kick-off before summer. We have four.
season_q2.5: Pollen season has taken out half the team. Stand-up turned into a sneezing session.
season_q2.6: It's June, and the client wants "just one small thing" before the holidays.

season_q3.1: The summer holidays are over and nobody remembers their passwords.
season_q3.2: Half the client is still at the cabin. We deploy in peace.
season_q3.3: I've been back for two days and have 412 unread emails.
season_q3.4: August is when everyone realises what they promised before the holidays.
season_q3.5: Autumn is here, and there are new budgets to fight over.
season_q3.6: Some people got a tan on holiday. The rest of us got it from coffee.

season_q4.1: The Christmas party is in three weeks and everyone has already picked an outfit.
season_q4.2: The client wants to spend the budget before New Year. We love December.
season_q4.3: The advent calendar in the kitchen is empty by the fourth.
season_q4.4: Everything has to be done "before Christmas". Nobody knows which Christmas.
season_q4.5: It's so dark I've started walking to work with a head torch.
season_q4.6: Someone has been playing Christmas music in the canteen since 1 November.

everyday.1: Someone took my yoghurt from the fridge. Again.
everyday.2: The meeting could have been an email. The email could have been nothing.
everyday.3: I wrote "just a quick one" in Slack and spent two hours on it.
everyday.4: Why are all our meeting rooms named after fjords?
everyday.5: The printer works, but only if you look at it.
everyday.6: I have three different time-tracking systems and one life.
everyday.7: Someone suggested doing stand-up sitting down. We discussed it for an hour.
everyday.8: The coffee machine has been named Kjell. Kjell has bad days.
everyday.9: I'm fairly sure "synergy" isn't a verb.
everyday.10: Someone is microwaving fish in the kitchen. We know who.
everyday.11: I've learned to say "it depends" with complete confidence.
everyday.12: We have a new whiteboard. Nobody dares rub out what's been on it since last week.
everyday.13: The Wi-Fi password is on a note in reception. That isn't security.
everyday.14: I tried the new standing desk. Now I stand and sit at the same time.
everyday.15: The client called it "a small change". It has three phases.
everyday.16: I'm currently an expert in two things: the client's domain and the canteen menu.
everyday.17: Who decided the Friday pizza should have pineapple? We demand answers.
everyday.18: I forgot to mute. Now everyone knows what I think of Excel.
everyday.19: We spent half an hour naming a variable. It's called "data".
everyday.20: Someone set up a channel for "important announcements". It's all memes.
everyday.21: I took a course in prompt engineering. Now I ask nicely for everything.
everyday.22: The code says "temporary fix". The date is 2021.
everyday.23: My mug from my last firm still raises questions.
everyday.24: I've decided to learn Vim. I've been in Vim since Tuesday.
everyday.25: The lift talks. Nobody knows who installed the voice.
everyday.26: I don't know what a "north star metric" is, but we have three.
everyday.27: The sticky notes from the workshop are still up. They've started to fall.
everyday.28: I've said "can you see my screen?" four times today. Nobody could.
everyday.29: Someone wrote "Who took the stapler?" on the whiteboard. It's a fair question.
everyday.30: The client wants it "like Spotify, but for groceries". We smile.
everyday.31: I've ordered a new laptop. Apparently it arrives next quarter.

ebike_scheme.title: Bike scheme
ebike_scheme.body: A group of employees has made a 34-slide deck on why you need an e-bike scheme.

friday_1655.title: Friday, 4:55 pm
friday_1655.body: {{customer}} is on the phone. Prod is down. Everyone is heading home.

genai_pivot.title: The board wants AI
genai_pivot.body: The board read an article and wants you to "do something with AI". What exactly is unclear.

choices.refuse: We'll keep doing what we're good at.

kickoff.title: Annual kick-off
kickoff.body: It's kick-off season. The social committee has strong opinions.

choices.lillestrom: A conference hotel off the motorway (NOK 3,000 per head)

competitor_cake.title: Cake war
competitor_cake.body: {{firm}} sent a cake with their logo to one of your clients. It was apparently delicious.

leaked_salary_sheet.title: Salary leak
leaked_salary_sheet.body: The salary spreadsheet ended up in the wrong Teams channel. 47 people saw it. Three took screenshots.

kofa_complaint.title: Procurement complaint
kofa_complaint.body: {{firm}} has filed a complaint about your contract award. They say you were "unrealistically cheap".

hackathon.title: Hackathon?
hackathon.body: Someone suggests an internal hackathon. There'll be pizza and at least one idea that goes nowhere.

conference_talk.title: Conference
conference_talk.body: One of your stars has been invited to speak at a tech conference.

burnout_wave.title: Burnout
burnout_wave.body: People are working too much. Some have started sleeping under their desks, and not because it's comfy.

choices.relief: Bring in help and give time off (NOK 300,000)

star_wants_remote.title: Remote work
star_wants_remote.body: {{name}} wants to work from a cabin in Lofoten. Full-time.

choices.grant: Fine, but we want northern lights on Teams.

acquisition_offer.title: Acquisition
acquisition_offer.body: A small agency with 8 good people is for sale. The owner just wants to go sailing.

influencer_post_viral.title: Viral!
influencer_post_viral.body: One of you wrote a post called "What kindergarten taught me about agile". It went viral.

office_ping_pong.title: Ping-pong table
office_ping_pong.body: Someone left a note in the suggestion box: "Ping-pong table?" It's the third one.

javazone_booth.title: Conference booth
javazone_booth.body: Booth registration for the big developer conference is open. Everyone else is getting one.

choices.booth: Big booth with a coffee bar (NOK 250,000)

tax_audit.title: Tax audit
tax_audit.body: The tax authority would like a chat about a few entries in your accounts. They're very polite.

glassdoor_review.title: Glassdoor
glassdoor_review.body: A former employee gave you one star on Glassdoor. The review is long and very accurate.

client_wants_chatbot.title: Chatbot
client_wants_chatbot.body: {{customer}} wants a chatbot. They don't know what it should do, but it has to ship before summer.

choices.no: Shall we start with the problem?

pizza_budget_cut.title: Pizza budget
pizza_budget_cut.body: Finance suggests cutting the pizza budget. It's a number nobody was supposed to know.

christmas_party.title: Christmas party
christmas_party.body: It's time for the Christmas party. Expectations are high after last year.

intern_program.title: Summer interns
intern_program.body: The university asks if you'd like summer interns. They're eager and know a little about everything.

open_source_fame.title: Open source
open_source_fame.body: A small library you built has reached 10,000 stars on GitHub.

cloud_credit_windfall.title: Cloud credits
cloud_credit_windfall.body: A cloud vendor gave you a pile of credits. Someone apparently needed to hit their target.

unionization.title: Union
unionization.body: Employees want to unionise. They've made a Miro board.

fagdag_vs_billable.title: Tech day or invoice?
fagdag_vs_billable.body: The tech day clashes with a client who wants people on Friday. What do you prioritise?

ceo_podcast.title: Podcast
ceo_podcast.body: The CEO has been invited onto a leadership podcast. It'll be 90 minutes.

rebranding_agency.title: Rebrand
rebranding_agency.body: An agency wants to give you a new visual identity. It involves a new font and a lot of orange.

wrong_reply_all.title: Reply all
wrong_reply_all.body: Someone hit reply-all on an email to the client. With a comment that wasn't meant for the client.

coffee_machine_broke.title: Coffee crisis
coffee_machine_broke.body: The coffee machine is broken. Productivity has dropped, and morale even more.

headhunter_calls.title: Headhunter
headhunter_calls.body: A headhunter has called {{name}} three times this week.

remote_debate.title: Office debate
remote_debate.body: There's a full-blown debate about remote work in #general. The thread has 312 replies.

poach_attempt.title: Afterwork alert
poach_attempt.body: {{firm}} took {{name}} out for drinks. It got late, and salaries were mentioned.

choices.match: Match the offer (+10% salary and half a quarter's pay)
choices.podcast: Cry about it on a CEO podcast

weak.extras: They had stars or a specialty you lacked.
weak.capacity: You didn't have enough people free.
weak.promise: Their promise about the start was more convincing.
weak.priority: The customer expected to matter more to them.
weak.luck: It was close, and luck decided it.

strong.effort: The bid was well put together.
strong.promise: Your promise about the start suited them.
strong.priority: They could tell this deal matters to you.
strong.luck: It was close, and luck was on your side.
strong.alone: Nobody else handed in an acceptable bid.

exposed.body: The thing you put in the drawer is out. A journalist called, and she had done her homework.

whistleblower.title: Complaint against {{name}}
whistleblower.gossip: Word is there's a whistleblowing case at {{firm}}. Nobody will say anything, everybody knows a bit.

report.body: HR has received a complaint about {{name}}, one of your best consultants. It's serious enough that it can't be ignored, and vague enough that nobody knows how bad it is.

choices.investigate: External investigation, and {{name}} sits out a quarter
choices.talk: Have a quiet word with {{name}} first
choices.drawer: Put it in a drawer. It'll blow over.

body.low: It turned out to be a misunderstanding that grew in a Slack thread. The complainant is relieved, {{name}} is embarrassed, and everyone learned something about tone.
body.high: It's not a misunderstanding. Several people on the team confirm the pattern, and now everyone is waiting to see what management does.

choices.clear: Close the case and move on
choices.mediate: Set up a mediation session with good coffee
choices.townhall: Take it to the all-hands, openly

team_feud.title: Feud in {{discipline}}
team_feud.gossip: Two seniors at {{firm}} are apparently no longer allowed on the same floor.

feud.body: Two seniors in {{discipline}} refuse to be in the same meeting. One has brought in their own coffee machine, the other has taken it personally. The team is splitting into camps.

choices.townhall: Gather everyone for an all-hands and talk it out
choices.split: Split the team for a while
choices.pick_side: Pick a side. One of them is right.
choices.wait: They're adults, they'll sort it out

body.low: They've started playing padel together. Nobody knows why, and nobody dares ask.
body.high: One of them has resigned, and two more are thinking of following. The coffee machine stays.

choices.celebrate: Buy the whole team Friday drinks
choices.move_on: Say nothing and enjoy the peace
choices.counteroffer: Make the leavers a better offer

client_exit.title: {{customer}} wants out
client_exit.gossip: {{firm}} is said to be losing a big client. Their head of sales was seen taking a long walk alone.

warning.body: {{customer}} calls: “We're considering ending the engagement.” They'll decide next quarter, and how happy they are with the work by then will settle it.

choices.send_partner: Send {{name}} to the client for a quarter
choices.rescue_meeting: Ask for a crisis meeting with the client
choices.graceful_exit: Thank them and end it in style

stayed.body: {{customer}} is staying. “We've seen the improvement,” they write, adding a smiley for the first time ever.

left.body: {{customer}} is ending the contract. The work stops now, and the team is on the bench from Monday.

choices.badmouth: Tell anyone who'll listen that they were impossible

client_insolvent.title: {{customer}} isn't paying
client_insolvent.gossip: One of {{firm}}'s clients is said to be in financial trouble. Their accountants have started reading the papers closely.

unpaid.body: {{customer}}'s invoice is unpaid, and their CFO isn't answering email. They might be in a temporary pinch. Or they might be done.

choices.keep_working: Keep working and show you can be trusted
choices.stop_work: Stop work until the money arrives
choices.factoring: Sell the invoice to a factoring company

body.low: The money arrived, with interest and a tin of biscuits. It was a messy reorganisation, not a bankruptcy.
body.high: {{customer}} has filed for bankruptcy. The invoices become a claim against the estate, and their team is out of work.

choices.hire_team: Hire two people from their team
choices.claim: Get a lawyer to file the claim

ai_act.title: The AI Act tightens
ai_act.news: The EU tightens the AI Act. Data projects across the country are on hold while the lawyers read.

ruling.body: New AI rules come into force, and clients freeze data projects while they work out what's allowed. Demand for data people drops for a few quarters.

choices.reskill: Train everyone on the rules and sell compliance

body.low: It blew over. The clients worked out that their “model” was a pivot table.
body.high: Second wave: clients want to renegotiate everything with the word “model” in it. Data models included.

choices.cut_prices: Give clients a discount on work in progress

krone_crash.title: The krone crashes
krone_crash.news: The krone drops like a stone. Cloud licences in dollars suddenly cost more than the consultants using them.

crash.body: The krone has fallen hard. Everything you buy in dollars and euros, from cloud licences to kit, costs more. Clients are tightening their belts and looking harder at price.

choices.hedge: Hedge the currency now, even if it costs
choices.pass_on: Pass the price rise on to clients

body.low: The bill arrived, and it was bearable. The CFO was seen smiling.
body.high: The bill arrived, and it was big. The licences auto-renewed in dollars, right at the bottom.

basement_flood.title: Basement flood
basement_flood.gossip: {{firm}}'s basement is apparently under water. The server room too.

flood.body: The basement is under water. So is the server room. And the beer fridge. The office is unusable for a good while.

choices.client_office: Ask {{customer}} if you can borrow some desks

body.low: The damage was smaller than feared, and the insurer wants paperwork before they pay.
body.high: The damage is worse than feared: the wiring in the walls has to go. The insurer wants paperwork for everything.

choices.forget: Forget it, we have better things to do

power_outage.title: Power cut
power_outage.gossip: {{firm}} has been without power for a week. Their consultants were spotted queueing at the nearest café.

dark.body: A storm has knocked out power across the district, and the grid company is saying “about a week”. The laptops have three hours of battery left.

choices.cabin: Everyone to the cabin, it has power
choices.pause: Take a break until the power's back

body.low: Nobody noticed. The clients had power cuts too.
body.high: An important delivery for {{customer}} slipped. They noticed.

data_leak.title: Data leak
data_leak.gossip: There's said to have been a data leak in one of {{firm}}'s teams. Their press contact is on holiday.

discovery.body: Customer data from {{customer}} has been sitting in a public storage bucket one of your teams set up. Nobody knows if anyone has seen it.

choices.disclose: Tell the client and the data protection authority right away
choices.forensics: Hire a security firm to find out what happened

body.low: The security firm is done: nobody downloaded anything. The bucket was open, but nobody walked in.
body.high: The security firm is done: the data was downloaded, several times, from a country you have no clients in.

choices.disclose: Tell the client and the authority

body.low: The client took it calmly, and the authority made a note. Now it's about showing you take it seriously.
body.high: It's in the papers. {{customer}} is furious, and the data protection authority wants a meeting.

choices.apology_tour: Go on an apology tour at {{customer}}
choices.lie_low: Keep a low profile until it blows over

ransomware.title: Ransomware
ransomware.gossip: {{firm}}'s timesheet system has reportedly been hit by ransomware. Their consultants have never been happier.

locked.body: The timesheet system from your supplier is encrypted. A polite note asks for bitcoin. Without timesheets you can't invoice.

choices.spreadsheets: Run on spreadsheets until it's sorted

body.low: Last year's backup works. Almost everything is back, apart from one long lunch nobody misses.
body.high: The backup is encrypted too. This quarter's timesheets are gone, and clients have to be invoiced on estimates.

choices.estimate_cautious: Invoice carefully. Better too little than too much.

prod_outage.title: Outage at {{customer}}
prod_outage.gossip: {{firm}} is said to have taken down production at a big client. On a Friday, naturally.

outage.body: Production at {{customer}} has been down for four hours. The logs point to a deploy from your team at 16:55 on Friday.

choices.war_room: War room: pull people off other work

body.low: It was a DNS problem on the client's side. It's always DNS.
body.high: It was you. A config change without review, right before the weekend.

choices.gracious: Help them fix it, without mentioning DNS
choices.told_you: Send a polite email titled “Root cause”
choices.own_it: Own it in a meeting with the client
choices.move_on: Move on and hope they forget

slack_slip.title: Wrong channel
slack_slip.gossip: A consultant at {{firm}} reportedly wrote something unfortunate in a client's Slack. The screenshot is doing the rounds.

message.body: One of your consultants wrote “this client is completely bonkers” in Slack. In the wrong channel. The client's channel, with {{customer}}'s leadership team in it.

choices.swap_consultant: Take the consultant off the engagement
choices.pretend: Delete it and hope nobody saw

body.low: The client found it quite funny. Deep down they apparently agree.
body.high: The client has escalated to the top. The message has been printed out and pinned up in a meeting room.

choices.cake: Send cake with a self-deprecating note

1.headline: New consultancy opens its doors
1.body:
{{firm}} has been registered and already has more vision statements than employees. The founders promise “a new way of doing consulting”, as founders do.

The first client is Kryptonitt. The rest will have to be won.

1.headline: Exodus at {{player}}
1.body:
{{count}} employees handed in their notice at {{player}} this quarter. Our sources point to everything from pay to the coffee machine.

HR says the farewell cake was “within budget”.

1.headline: New faces in the corridors at {{player}}
1.body:
{{count}} new consultants have received an access card, a laptop and a branded hoodie. The first week goes on onboarding and on finding out where the printer paper lives.

They start billing next quarter.

1.headline: Star leaves {{firm}}
1.body:
{{name}} has said goodbye to {{firm}}. The farewell post on LinkedIn already has hundreds of reactions, including a suspicious number of hearts from rivals.

Where they are headed next is not yet known.

1.headline: A talent on the rise
1.body:
Colleagues describe {{name}} as “the one you ask when nobody else knows”. Management at {{player}} has reportedly started talking about a future as a star in {{discipline}}.

{{name}} says it's just a matter of reading the documentation.

1.headline: A promise kept
1.body:
When {{name}} had a career talk at {{player}}, growth was promised. Now it has happened, which is not an everyday event in this industry.

Colleagues report a better mood by the coffee machine.

1.headline: A broken promise comes at a cost
1.body:
{{name}} has left {{player}}. According to sources, growth was promised in a career talk a year ago, but little happened.

The rest of the department has taken note.

1.headline: Homegrown star
1.body:
{{player}} has promoted {{name}} to star consultant in {{discipline}}. It's rare for a consultancy to grow its stars rather than buy them.

The promotion was celebrated with cake and a speech that ran slightly long.

1.headline: Certificates in hand
1.body_one:
{{name}} has finished the course and already posted the certificate on LinkedIn. The instructor describes them as “engaged, occasionally too engaged”.

The knowledge is meant to benefit the clients.
1.body_other:
{{count}} people at {{player}} finished courses this quarter. Their LinkedIn feeds now consist mostly of certificates.

The knowledge is meant to benefit the clients.

1.headline: Nobody wanted the job
1.body:
The tender from {{customer}} did not receive a single bid. Procurement is now considering whether a 140-page requirements document was a bit much.

What happens next is unclear.

1.headline: {{customer}} turns everyone down
1.body:
None of the bids for the {{customer}} tender made the cut. The client reportedly asked for “something more than a logo and a recycled CV”.

The contract will not be awarded this time.

1.headline: Rejected on quality
1.body:
{{customer}} has rejected the bid from {{player}}. The evaluation points to weak quality, though it praises the colour scheme on the cover.

More experienced people and more effort on the bid could help next time.

1.headline: The client checked capacity
1.body:
{{customer}} rejected the bid from {{player}} because the firm didn't have enough people free. The client apparently rang around and asked.

It pays to bid where you actually have people on the bench.

1.headline: {{player}} wins at {{customer}}
1.body:
{{player}} came out on top in the {{customer}} tender. There were {{bidders}} bids. {{strong}}

The win was celebrated at the office with pizza and a gong that was slightly too loud.

1.headline: A place on the framework
1.body:
{{player}} has been ranked number {{rank}} on the framework agreement with {{customer}}. {{strong}}

A framework is no guarantee of work, but it's a foot in the door.

1.headline: {{firm}} takes the contract
1.body:
{{player}} lost the {{customer}} tender to {{firm}}. {{weak}}

The sales team has already started on the next bid.

1.headline: Close, but not enough
1.body:
{{player}} lost the {{customer}} tender to {{firm}}. {{weak}} {{strong}}

It was close, but close doesn't bill any hours.

1.headline: {{firm}} wins at {{customer}}
1.body:
{{firm}} has been awarded the {{customer}} contract, beating {{bidders}} others. The client points to “a solid understanding of our needs”.

The competitors are considering an appeal but haven't made up their minds.

2.headline: New contract for {{firm}}
2.body:
{{customer}} has picked {{firm}}. {{bidders}} other firms bid, but had to accept defeat.

Insiders say it came down to price and experience. {{firm}} says it came down to culture.

3.headline: {{customer}} picks a supplier
3.body:
After a long evaluation, {{customer}} has settled on {{firm}}. {{bidders}} others competed for the work.

The work starts soon, and the job ads are already out.

1.headline: {{firm}} tops the framework
1.body:
{{firm}} has been ranked first on the new framework agreement with {{customer}}. {{bidders}} firms competed for the places.

Whoever ranks first usually gets the first call-offs.

2.headline: Framework settled at {{customer}}
2.body:
{{customer}} has ranked the suppliers on its new framework agreement, and {{firm}} took first place. {{bidders}} firms took part in total.

The losers console themselves that a framework guarantees nothing.

1.headline: {{customer}} drops {{firm}}
1.body:
{{customer}} has ended its contract with {{firm}} early. The press release says the client is “going in a different direction”.

Sources describe the relationship as “demanding for both sides, mostly for us”.

1.headline: The {{customer}} engagement is over
1.body:
The work between {{player}} and {{customer}} has ended as planned. The client gave {{satisfaction}} out of 100 in the final satisfaction survey.

The consultants are back at the office, looking for the next engagement.

1.headline: {{customer}} wants more
1.body:
{{customer}} is extending its contract with {{player}} by {{count}} quarters without a new tender. The client is happy, and it saves everyone another procurement round.

Procurement is particularly pleased about the last part.

1.headline: New rate at {{customer}}
1.body:
{{player}} has negotiated a new hourly rate with {{customer}}, now ×{{rate}}. The client said yes after two meetings and a long pause.

The head of procurement reportedly sighed audibly.

1.headline: No to a new rate
1.body:
{{customer}} turned down the request from {{player}} for a higher rate. The client considers the current rate “more than fair”.

The relationship is a little cooler after the meeting.

1.headline: {{player}} walks away from {{customer}}
1.body:
{{player}} has cancelled its contract with {{customer}} and paid the break fee. Both sides describe the split as “orderly”.

The industry notices when a consultancy walks away of its own accord.

1.headline: {{customer}} grows the team
1.body:
{{customer}} is bringing in {{count}} more consultants from {{player}} in {{discipline}}. The project is growing, and so is the invoice.

The newcomers start this quarter.

1.headline: No budget at {{customer}}
1.body:
{{player}} offered {{customer}} more people, but the client has no budget right now. Satisfaction took a small knock from the request.

The client asks to be contacted again “after the budget round”.

1.headline: {{name}} switches sides
1.body:
{{name}} is moving from {{from}} to {{to}}. The move was reportedly agreed at an afterwork with a remarkably good atmosphere.

{{from}} declined to comment.

1.headline: Pricey afterwork, no payoff
1.body:
An afterwork with people from {{from}} ended with a large bill and no new hires. The guests thanked everyone for the food and went back to their jobs.

The bill has been filed as “networking”.

1.headline: Rumours swirl around {{player}}
1.body:
Rumours about {{player}} are doing the rounds in the industry. Nobody knows who started them, but everyone has heard them.

Clients have started asking questions in meetings.

1.headline: Revealed: how {{firm}} really works
1.body:
Internal documents show how {{firm}} is really run. The story is behind a paywall, but nobody in the industry is talking about anything else.

{{firm}} calls the leak “taken out of context”.

1.headline: {{firm}} caught snooping
1.body:
{{firm}} obtained its rivals' bids by improper means. The firm has been fined {{fine}}.

The CEO apologises and promises “a review of our procedures”.

1.headline: Payslips gone astray
1.body:
{{firm}} has been collecting payslips from employees at {{target}}. Asking isn't illegal, but it isn't pretty either.

Staff at {{target}} say they feel “surveyed”.

1.headline: Mole uncovered at {{target}}
1.body:
A “trainee” at {{target}} turned out to be working for {{firm}}. They had been there four months and had become popular at lunch.

{{firm}} has been fined {{fine}}.

1.headline: An afterwork with an agenda
1.body:
{{firm}} has invited staff from {{target}} to afterworks so often that people have noticed. {{target}} calls it “systematic”.

{{firm}} says it simply enjoys social occasions.

1.headline: The team was in another time zone
1.body:
{{customer}} discovered that the work delivered by {{firm}} was done by a different team abroad. The contract has been terminated and {{firm}} has been fined {{fine}}.

Suspicions arose when stand-up always started at four in the morning.

1.headline: Padded CVs exposed
1.body:
{{customer}} checked the CVs {{firm}} used in its bid and found experience that doesn't exist. One consultant had apparently worked with Kubernetes since before it was invented.

The contract is lost.

1.headline: Consultants who don't exist
1.body:
{{firm}} offered {{customer}} consultants who do not exist. It came to light when the client asked to meet the team.

{{firm}} has been fined {{fine}}.

1.headline: Promised seniors, delivered juniors
1.body:
{{customer}} got juniors instead of the seniors {{firm}} promised in its bid. The juniors are doing their best, but it's not what the client paid for.

The relationship is described as frosty.

1.headline: The rumours came from {{firm}}
1.body:
The rumours about {{target}} in recent months have been traced back to {{firm}}. Nobody is especially surprised, but everyone is a little embarrassed on the industry's behalf.

{{firm}} has no comment.

1.headline: Leak traced to {{firm}}
1.body:
The leak about {{target}} to the press came from {{firm}}. The firm has been fined {{fine}}.

The paper that got the tip is not commenting.

1.headline: LinkedIn post backfires
1.body:
A post by {{firm}} about {{target}} has been shared thousands of times, mostly with rolled eyes. The comments are not on {{firm}}'s side.

The post has been deleted, but the screenshots live on.

1.headline: {{firm}} has the best engineering culture
1.body:
The jury named {{firm}} Best Engineering Culture {{year}} for its tech days, courses and an internal Slack channel people actually read.

The award was accepted by a group in hoodies who gave a speech about test coverage.

1.headline: The industry's best coffee
1.body:
{{firm}} wins Best Coffee Machine in the Industry {{year}}. The jury highlights a steady temperature, good crema and a machine that is “never broken on a Monday”.

It is widely considered the industry's most coveted award.

1.headline: Tender champion: {{firm}}
1.body:
Nobody won more tenders than {{firm}} in {{year}}. The bid team has worked a lot of late evenings and drunk a lot of coffee.

The competitors are wondering what the secret is.

1.headline: Rocket growth at {{firm}}
1.body:
{{firm}} has been named Rocket Growth {{year}}. The firm has grown so fast that half the staff still don't know where the meeting rooms are.

The jury praises growth that is both fast and profitable.

1.headline: Creative timesheets honoured
1.body:
{{firm}} receives the award for Most Creative Timesheets {{year}}. The jury was impressed by how many hours fit into an ordinary day.

The auditors have asked for a meeting.

1.headline: Glassdoor disaster of the year
1.body:
{{firm}} has been named Glassdoor Disaster of the Year {{year}}. The reviews are mostly about overtime and a missing fruit bowl.

Management says it “takes the feedback seriously”.

1.headline: New trend: {{trend}}
1.body:
The industry has a new buzzword: {{trend}}. Demand for consultants is shifting, and some disciplines will feel it more than others.

Analysts expect the trend to last a while. They expect that of every trend.

2.headline: Everyone is talking about {{trend}}
2.body:
“{{trend}}” is on everyone's lips in the industry. Boards across the country are asking management what it means for them.

For consultancies, it means new opportunities for some and thinner order books for others.

1.headline: Goodbye to {{trend}}
1.body:
The “{{trend}}” trend is over, and the market is returning to normal. The consultants who posted about it on LinkedIn have moved on to the next topic.

The next trend is probably already on its way.

1.headline: {{firm}} buys an agency
1.body:
{{firm}} has bought a small {{discipline}} agency with eight employees. The new colleagues move in next week.

The business cards have already been reprinted.

1.headline: {{firm}} goes bankrupt
1.body:
{{firm}} has filed for bankruptcy. Clients have been told their contracts will go out to tender again.

The foosball table and three coffee machines are up for sale online.

2.headline: The end for {{firm}}
2.body:
After several difficult quarters, it's over for {{firm}}. The bank pulled the credit line, and the board saw no other way out.

The consultants are already talking to competitors.

1.headline: {{firm}} goes bankrupt
1.body:
{{firm}} has gone bankrupt. The receiver has taken over the office, the clients and the foosball table.

The founders thank everyone for the journey on LinkedIn.

1.headline: The bank calls {{player}}
1.body:
{{player}} has been below its credit limit for a quarter, and the bank has been in touch. The tone was polite, but no longer warm.

Two quarters in a row, and it's over.

1.headline: {{buyer}} buys {{firm}}
1.body:
{{buyer}} has bought {{firm}}, with its people, clients and contracts. The logo will be “kept for now”.

The staff have received new email addresses and a welcome pack with socks.

1.headline: {{player}} moves up
1.body:
{{player}} has reached level {{level}} and is moving into bigger offices. The removal company reports an unusual number of plants.

New opportunities come with the level.

1.headline: Goal reached: {{mission}}
1.body:
{{player}} has reached the goal “{{mission}}”. The board applauded politely and entered it in the minutes.

Chair Bjørn says he knew it all along.

1.headline: {{firm}} goes public
1.body:
{{firm}} was listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange today. The founders rang the bell, and someone filmed it vertically.

From now on, every quarter has to beat the last.

1.headline: Disappointing quarter for {{player}}
1.body:
{{player}} delivered a weaker quarter than the last, and the share price fell. Analysts are using words like “concerning”.

The mood in the corridors is subdued.

1.headline: {{player}} beats expectations
1.body:
{{player}} delivered a better quarter than the last, and the share price rose. Analysts are pleased, at least until the next quarter.

Someone in finance has bought cake.

1.headline: A full team from day one
1.body:
{{player}} promised {{customer}} the whole team from day one, and delivered. The client says it's “not what you usually get in this industry”.

Satisfaction and the relationship have both improved.

1.headline: A phased start, as promised
1.body:
The start at {{customer}} was phased, just as {{player}} promised in its bid. The client appreciates predictability.

The project manager describes the start as “undramatic, in a good way”.

1.headline: The discovery phase is done
1.body:
{{player}} has delivered the discovery work at {{customer}}, and the client is glad someone asked before starting. Full rates apply from now on.

The 60-page report will apparently be read.

1.headline: The full-team promise didn't hold
1.body:
{{player}} promised {{customer}} the whole team from the start, but had to fill the gaps with contractors. The client has taken note.

Satisfaction and the relationship have both taken a knock.

1.headline: Phased turned into outsourced
1.body:
{{player}} promised {{customer}} a phased start with its own people, but more than half the seats were filled by contractors. The client is disappointed.

Satisfaction and the relationship have both taken a knock.

1.headline: Crisis at {{player}}: {{crisis}}
1.body:
{{player}} is in the middle of a crisis: {{crisis}}. Management has called a meeting, and the coffee is extra strong.

How it's handled will decide how deep the marks go. See the overview.

1.headline: Filed away
1.body:
The “{{crisis}}” matter at {{player}} has been hushed up. For now, nobody outside the firm knows.

Drawers have a habit of being opened again.

1.headline: {{player}} comes out stronger
1.body:
The “{{crisis}}” matter is over, and {{player}} handled it well. Staff and clients praise the openness.

The crisis will probably be used as an example at the next leadership offsite.

1.headline: It could have been worse
1.body:
The “{{crisis}}” matter is over for {{player}}. It didn't go perfectly, but it went.

Management has promised “lessons learned”.

1.headline: The crisis left its mark
1.body:
The “{{crisis}}” matter is over, but {{player}} did not come out of it well. Staff and clients have both noticed.

It will take time to rebuild trust.

1.headline: It all came out for {{player}}
1.body:
The “{{crisis}}” matter that {{player}} tried to hush up is now in the papers. Keeping it quiet has made it worse.

Clients are calling, and the heat is rising.

1.headline: {{firm}} tried to hide a problem
1.body:
{{firm}} tried to hush up the “{{crisis}}” matter, but now it's out. Sources say management knew for a long time.

{{firm}}'s clients are asking for explanations.

1.headline: Whistleblowing case at {{firm}}?
1.body:
Several sources describe an internal whistleblowing case at {{firm}}. Management will confirm nothing, but the meeting rooms are booked all week.

What the case concerns is not known.

1.headline: Trouble at {{firm}}
1.body:
Two senior {{discipline}} people at {{firm}} are said to have stopped speaking to each other. One has reportedly moved to a different floor.

Colleagues describe the atmosphere as “a Christmas party with no music”.

1.headline: Big client leaving {{firm}}?
1.body:
{{firm}} is said to be on the verge of losing a major client. The head of sales was seen taking a long walk alone at lunch.

{{firm}} does not comment on client relationships.

1.headline: Payment trouble at a {{firm}} client
1.body:
One of {{firm}}'s clients is said to be struggling to pay its bills. The finance department has started reading the bankruptcy notices closely.

How much is at stake is not known.

1.headline: EU tightens the AI Act
1.body:
New rules from Brussels put data projects across the country on hold. The lawyers are reading, and the consultants are waiting.

The industry expects it to take a few quarters before the market recovers.

1.headline: The krone in free fall
1.body:
The Norwegian krone has fallen sharply against the dollar and the euro. Cloud licences and software priced in dollars have suddenly become far more expensive.

Several clients have put new projects on hold.

1.headline: Water in the basement at {{firm}}
1.body:
{{firm}}'s basement is under water, and the server room with it. The consultants are working from home while the dehumidifiers run.

The insurer has sent an assessor and a pair of wellies.

1.headline: Lights out at {{firm}}
1.body:
{{firm}} has been without power for a week. The consultants have moved to the nearest café, which reports record takings.

The grid company promises power “shortly”.

1.headline: Data leak at {{firm}}?
1.body:
Data from one of {{firm}}'s teams has reportedly gone astray. It's unclear how much has leaked, and who is affected.

The press officer is on holiday and not answering the phone.

1.headline: Ransomware hits {{firm}}
1.body:
{{firm}}'s timesheet system has been encrypted by ransomware. The attackers are demanding payment in cryptocurrency.

The consultants have rarely been happier.

1.headline: Outage at a {{firm}} client
1.body:
{{firm}} has reportedly taken down production at a major client. It happened on a Friday afternoon, of course.

The client is not pleased, and an incident report is being written.

1.headline: Unfortunate message, wrong channel
1.body:
A consultant at {{firm}} reportedly wrote something unfortunate in a client's Slack, thinking it was the internal channel. The screenshot is doing the rounds.

{{firm}} has apologised.
